newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo Corp says no comment on Black statement.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Corp says no comment on Black statement.

text.p: Japanese trading house Sumitomo Corp said on Tuesday that it had no comment on a statement by Canada-based scrap trader Herbert Black that Sumitomo still holds a copper long position of 500,000 tonnes.
"We make absolutely no comments on our positions," a Sumitomo spokesman said when asked about Black's statement, which was made at a metal industry luncheon in London on Monday.
Black, president of American Iron and Metal Co, also said he was "confident (Sumitomo's) position has not been unwound".
Black is thought to be one of the traders who broke Sumitomo's grip on the copper market earlier this year.
He said the Japanese trading giant holds 500,000 tonnes of copper and forecast its copper trading losses would eventually rise to $3 to $4 billion.

Sumitomo announced on September 19 that its estimated losses from unauthorised copper trading, stemming from deals by its former star copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka, had risen to $2.6 billion, up from its initial estimate in June of $1.8 billion.
The trade house also said at that time, however, that it had nearly completed the liquidation of its open copper positions and did not expect any further revisions to the estimated loss.

Sumitomo officials have repeatedly declined to comment on the extent of the remaining open positions or into whose hands positions may have been transferred, noting that the market is very sensitive to this subject.

In the September 19 announcement, Sumitomo president Kenji Miyahara said: "There still remain some positions, including both short and long positions, but the liquidation of open positions is nearly complete."
Black's comments weighed on copper prices on Monday.

The London Metal Exchange benchmark three-month copper price dipped to a low of $1,900 a tonne in London afternoon trade before recovering to close at $1,905, off $6. In Asian morning trade on Tuesday, copper was quoted at $1,895/$1,900.
LME three-month copper has held to a range of $1,850 to $1,990 for the past month, consolidating after crashing in the wake of Sumitomo's announcement in June of its trading losses.
